privacy.title: Privacy and personal data
privacy.lede: We wrote this page in plain language. When in doubt, we handle less data.

collect.title: What data we handle
collect.text: This site has no accounts or forms of its own. If you register, write to us or join the directory, you do it through external forms (Google Forms or Tally) or by email; that data does not pass through this site.

analytics.title: Cookie-free analytics
analytics.text: We use Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights to measure visits and performance. They use no cookies and do not follow people across sites. We use no third-party tracking pixels.

purpose.title: What we use it for
purpose.text: Only to manage your registration, answer your questions and, if you authorize it, show you in the leaders’ directory.

directory.title: Leaders’ directory
directory.text: Appearing is voluntary and based on informed consent. You choose the visibility level: public (name, organization and LinkedIn), initials (only initials, province and topics) or hidden (you count on the map but do not appear in the list). We show the province at most: never district, community, coordinates or address, and we do not publish phone numbers or emails. The “Request contact” button goes through the team, who ask you before connecting. Every profile is reviewed manually before it is published.

withdraw.title: How to withdraw your data
withdraw.text: You can ask us to remove your data from the directory by writing to the project email. We commit to removing it within 72 hours at most.

images.title: Photos and videos
images.text: We only publish photos and videos of people who gave their written consent for the use of their image.

law.title: Legal framework
law.text: We handle personal data in accordance with Peru’s Law No. 29733, the Personal Data Protection Law.

project.title: Five Fulbright alumni, one youth network against illegal mining
project.lede: PACTO-MI is the Platform for Action against Illegal Mining: a project that trains and connects young people and leaders in Cajamarca and Madre de Dios.
project.sponsorLine: 2025 Alumni Engagement Innovation Fund (AEIF) winner, sponsored by the U.S. Embassy in Peru.

origin.title: Why we decided to act
origin.p1: PACTO-MI was born from five Fulbright alumni from Cajamarca who identified an information gap about illegal mining in communities and universities, and decided to act.
origin.p2: Sponsored by the U.S. Embassy in Peru, we train young people and leaders with rigorous knowledge, practical tools and an action network.

mission.label: Mission
mission.text: To train and connect young people and community leaders in Cajamarca and Madre de Dios with rigorous knowledge, practical tools and an action network, so they can prevent illegal mining and its ties to organized crime and strengthen formal mining that is responsible to the land and its people.

vision.label: Vision
vision.text: A youth network present in every Peruvian region affected by illegal mining, turning outrage into informed civic action and serving as a reference across Latin America for the defense of territory.

goal.label: General objective
goal.text: To create a Youth Action Network to combat illegal mining and its ties to organized crime by empowering at least 300 youth and community leaders with the knowledge, tools, and skills needed for effective prevention and advocacy.

evidence.name: Evidence
evidence.text: We speak with data and verifiable sources.

territory.name: Territory
territory.text: We start from each community’s reality, in the Andes and the Amazon.

youth.name: Youth-led
youth.text: Young people are not an audience: they lead.

articulation.name: Collaboration
articulation.text: Public sector, formal industry, academia and civil society at the same table.

care.name: Care
care.text: We protect the safety and data of everyone who takes part.

aeif.title: About the AEIF
aeif.p1: The Alumni Engagement Innovation Fund (AEIF) is a U.S. Department of State initiative, implemented in Peru by the U.S. Embassy, that funds projects led by exchange program alumni.
aeif.p2: Proposals go through a national and a global review. In 2025, the team of five alumni from Cajamarca who created PACTO-MI was selected at both stages.

fronts.title: Four lines of work
fronts.f1: In-person meetings in Cajamarca and Madre de Dios with community leaders and the public and private sectors.
fronts.f2: Digital campaigns to show the impact and the spread of illegal mining.
fronts.f3: Strategic collaboration with academic, scientific and business partners.
fronts.f4: Community action and youth leadership, turning social outrage into active participation.
